# Home

I am an interdisciplinary scholar affiliated with the [Faculty of Social Sciences, Charles University](https://fsv.cuni.cz/en) in Prague. My research draws upon my background in economics, philosophy, and political theory, focusing on the impacts of generative AI on political and educational institutions.

[Research](https://petrspecian.com/research.html) [Publications](https://petrspecian.com/publications.html) [Contact](https://petrspecian.com/contact.html)

I serve as the Coordinator for Studies at [PPE Prague](https://studyppe.com/) at the Institute of Political Studies. I teach and write in Czech and English.

![Petr Špecián, photographed in a white shirt against a plain background](https://petrspecian.com/assets/petr-specian.jpg)

## Research

I seek ways to expedite institutional adaptation to technological shocks and improve the robustness and performance of our key institutional infrastructure. I am also interested in futures studies and progress studies.

Research programme

### AI institutional transformation

How universities and democratic institutions can harness AI’s benefits while preserving the human epistemic agency essential to democratic societies.

[See the programme →](https://petrspecian.com/research.html#ai-institutional-transformation)

Journal article · Social Epistemology

### Machine Advisors

Large language models can access more information than human experts and tailor their findings to individuals’ needs. Could their use broaden the access of democratic assemblies to expert knowledge?

[Read the overview →](https://petrspecian.com/publications/machine-advisors.html)

Funded project · 2024–2026

### Look Who’s Talking?

What epistemic effects can be expected of LLMs in democratic settings, and how can we improve the odds that this technology will serve democracy rather than harm it?

[View the project →](https://petrspecian.com/research.html#look-whos-talking)

## Book

Published by Routledge, my first book *Behavioral Political Economy and Democratic Theory: Fortifying Democracy for the Digital Age* examines the friction between modern technology and human rationality within liberal democracies. As we move further into a digitally-driven information age, challenges such as disinformation and extreme political polarization become more prominent.

Using a behavioral economics approach, the book explores solutions to these issues while maintaining democratic values and optimizing democratic decision-making. It advocates for a behaviorally grounded theory of democracy and discusses how our understanding of human rationality’s limitations can help shape robust democratic institutions.

[About the book](https://petrspecian.com/publications/book.html) · [Publisher page](https://www.routledge.com/Behavioral-Political-Economy-and-Democratic-Theory-Fortifying-Democracy/Specian/p/book/9781032229737)
